title: The Best French Press Coffee Makers on Amazon
excerpt: Glass or steel, big or small: three French presses worth buying, plus the 4-minute method that makes them shine.

body.p: A French press is the simplest way to make rich, full-bodied coffee. There's no paper filter, so more of the coffee's oils end up in your cup. There's also nothing electronic to break. You need coarse grounds, hot water and four minutes. The differences between presses come down to material, filter quality and size.

body.h: Best overall: Veken 34 oz French Press

body.p: The Veken is one of the most popular French presses on Amazon, and it gets the details right. The carafe is thick borosilicate glass, and the plunger uses a four-layer stainless steel filter (a spiral plate, a cross plate and two fine mesh screens) to keep sludge out of your cup. No plastic touches the coffee while it brews. It comes apart easily for cleaning, and the 34 oz size makes about four mugs.

body.h: Best unbreakable option: Utopia Kitchen Stainless Steel

body.p: Glass presses break. If yours lives near a busy sink or goes camping, the Utopia Kitchen press is made from double-walled 304 stainless steel, which keeps coffee hot noticeably longer and survives drops. It also has a four-layer filter and comes apart fully for washing. The trade-off is that you can't see the brew inside.

body.h: Best for one: Bodum Chambord, 12 oz

body.p: Bodum's Chambord is the design most people picture when they think of a French press, and it's still made in Portugal. The 12 oz size brews one large mug or two small cups, which is ideal if you're the only coffee drinker at home and don't want leftovers going cold.

body.h: How to make great French press coffee

ul: Use a coarse grind, about 1 tablespoon of coffee per 4 oz of water (roughly 1:15).
Pour water just off the boil (about 200°F) over the grounds and stir gently.
Put the lid on and wait 4 minutes.
Press slowly and steadily, then pour everything out right away so it doesn't keep brewing and turn bitter.

body.p: Fine grounds are the number one cause of muddy French press coffee. A burr grinder set to coarse fixes it. See our guide to the best burr coffee grinders.
